body:
Aguilar 393.36, Brenthany 343.56. The single-week swing was 49.80 points in Still Jerry's favor — more than enough to erase the 18.43 he started Christmas Eve down — and the cumulative result is the kind of two-week final that reshuffles a league's understanding of itself: **Aguilar 807.80, Brenthany 776.43, by 31.37**. Aguilar gets the trophy. Brenthany gets to spend the offseason replaying every Week-17 lineup decision they made.

The matter, when you walk it back, is not that Aguilar did anything bizarre. He did exactly what his roster has always threatened to do.

**Brock Purdy** went for 45.95 in San Francisco's wild 42-38 Sunday-night win over Chicago — five total touchdowns from Purdy in a game that was tied at 7, 14, 21, 28, *and* 35 before the 49ers won it on a 38-yard scoring strike to Jauan Jennings. The first 49ers game ever to be tied at five separate scores. Aguilar started him. **Dak Prescott** added 28.01 on Christmas Day in a 30-23 Cowboys win over Washington, and that one game also coughed up a tidy 15.05 from George Pickens (lead-retaking 38-yard touchdown reception) and 15.33 from Brandon Aubrey just because. The 49ers-Bears game spit out 24.15 from D'Andre Swift on the way past.

That's just the offense. The IDPs were the real story.

**Chase Young**, in his Saints uniform, returned a strip-sack 33 yards for a touchdown against Tennessee. **37.95 fantasy points.** A career line for a player half this league had given up on after the Washington years. **DeMarcus Lawrence** went off in Seattle's 27-10 thumping of Carolina — six tackles, a forced fumble *and* a recovery, his sixth sack of the season. 25.18 points. And **Mike Jackson**, the same Carolina cornerback Lawrence was playing against, posted a career-high 11 tackles, two pass deflections, and his fourth interception of the year on the losing side of that same field. 28.93. Aguilar got 92 IDP points off three players and *both teams* of one football game. That doesn't happen. That happened.

For Brenthany, the disaster wasn't on defense. **Aidan Hutchinson** delivered (31.08 on two sacks of Max Brosmer to push his season total to 13.5, tied for third-most in Lions history). **Andrew Van Ginkel** delivered (26.25 — 1.5 sacks and *two* fumble recoveries on Christmas Day in the Vikings' upset of Detroit, where Brenthany owned both sidelines). **T.J. Edwards** delivered, with maybe the most dramatic single play of the entire week — a 34-yard pick-six off Brock Purdy on the Bears' opening defensive snap, returned in fifteen elapsed seconds. 32.15.

Three Brenthany IDPs combined for 89.48 points. In any other week this season, that's the championship.

The disaster was on offense. **Puka Nacua** dropped from 50.00 in Week 16 to 14.95 in Week 17 — caught a tying 11-yard touchdown with 2:46 left on Monday Night, had a 41-yard score wiped out by a holding penalty, and the Rams lost 27-24 to Atlanta on a late field goal anyway. **Joe Burrow** posted 29.42 on a Bengals win, fine, but a 12-point regression from his 41.61 the week prior. **Trevor Lawrence** dropped to 26.75 with a pair of rushing touchdowns saving an otherwise ugly 23-of-37, no-passing-touchdown line in Jacksonville's win over Indianapolis. **Jonathan Taylor** logged his 18th rushing touchdown of the season — 19.65 was *fine*, but it wasn't the thirty-burger he'd been threatening every other Sunday in his stealth MVP campaign.

Brenthany's offensive stars, week-over-week: **negative 89.31 points.** The IDPs alone weren't enough to absorb that.

There is a version of this league's history where Karma Cowboy puts up the same 432.87 they hung on the field two weeks running and walks away undefeated through the playoffs. That was, by any reasonable read of the data, the most likely outcome going into Christmas. It is not the version that happened. The version that happened is that Aguilar's seven-month case for *ceiling beats consistency* finally got cashed in the one week of the year where it counts the most.

Aguilar finished the regular season 15-11. He was the four-seed. He played a Wild Card week to even *get* to the championship round. He spent two months losing close games to teams that were starting better quarterbacks than his. And on the Sunday after Christmas, every variance position on his roster hit at the same time, and the league's runaway favorite ran out of math. **Still Jerry's Team are your 2025 Brisket champions.**
kicker: Brenthany hung 432.87 and lost. They will spend a year asking what they should have done differently. The honest answer: nothing. They got beat by a roster having its best week of the season at the worst possible time.
lede: There is, somewhere in Aguilar's house, a screenshot of 432.87 — the score that, for seven days, looked like the only number that mattered. He should keep it; on Sunday the league found out two-week championships are decided in the second week.
title: The Christmas comeback: Still Jerry's Team are 2025 Brisket champs
